SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE.text: Spring profile. `prod` turns on production behaviour: no default passwords, secure cookies, payments refuse to run in simulated mode. Set by Helm on AWS.

SERVER_PORT.text: Port the service listens on. Each service has its own default (gateway 8080, auth 8081, product 8082 ... support 8092).

MANAGEMENT_SERVER_PORT.text: Port for actuator (health, metrics). Equal to the service port for every service except the gateway, whose `prod` profile uses a separate port 8081.

MANAGEMENT_SERVER_ADDRESS.text: Bind address for a separate management port. The gateway defaults to `127.0.0.1` in `prod`, which Kubernetes probes cannot reach; the chart sets `0.0.0.0`.

SPRING_CONFIG_ADDITIONAL_LOCATION.text: Extra config directory. On AWS it points at `/config/`, where the discovery ConfigMap is mounted.

SPRING_LIFECYCLE_TIMEOUT_PER_SHUTDOWN_PH.text: How long a pod may spend finishing in-flight requests on shutdown. Must be shorter than the pod termination grace period.

SERVER_FORWARD_HEADERS_STRATEGY.text: Makes auth-service honour `X-Forwarded-Host/Proto`, so the Google sign-in callback URL uses the public host instead of the internal one.

RATING_MEDIA_DIR.text: Directory where review images are stored. On AWS this is an EBS volume, which is why rating-service runs one replica.

STOREFRONT_BASE_URL.text: Public origin of the storefront. Used in links inside emails (verify, reset password, order, referral) and as a CORS/redirect reference.

ADMIN_BASE_URL.text: Public origin of the admin / seller portal. Used in seller emails.

SPRING_DATASOURCE_HIKARI_MAXIMUM_POOL_SI.text: Maximum database connections per pod (the code default is 10; the AWS chart uses 8). Pods x this value, summed over all services, must stay below the database `max_connections`.

SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL.text: JDBC URL of the service's own database. On AWS it ends in `?sslmode=require` (RDS refuses unencrypted connections).

SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME.text: Database role of the service (`<name>_service`), created by the database bootstrap.

SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD.text: Password of that role. **No default in the `prod` profile.** On AWS it comes from Secrets Manager (`<project>-<env>/db`).

AUTH_JWT_ISSUER.text: Token issuer (`iss`). Must be identical in auth-service, the gateway and every resource server, or every request fails with `invalid_token`.

AUTH_JWT_AUDIENCES.text: Token audience (`aud`). Same rule as the issuer.

PLATFORM_JWT_KEYSTORE_PATH.text: Path of the PKCS#12 keystore holding the JWT signing key. Mounted, never baked into an image.

PLATFORM_JWT_KEYSTORE_ALIAS.text: Alias of the key used for signing. May be blank while the keystore has one key; set it during a key rotation.

AUTH_DATA_KEY.text: AES-256 key (base64, 32 bytes) that encrypts two-factor secrets at rest. Blank: the service starts, but enabling two-factor fails. Losing or changing it locks existing 2FA users out.

AUTH_STATE_COOKIE_SECRET.text: Signs the OIDC `state` cookie. Must be the same on every auth-service replica.

AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE.text: Marks the refresh-token cookie `Secure` (HTTPS only). `true` everywhere except local HTTP.

AUTH_REGISTRATION_ENABLED.text: Allows self-service sign-up. Default `false`; the local template and the AWS chart turn it on so you can register the first admin. Turn it off again once your accounts exist.

AUTH_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_URIS.text: Comma-separated exact URLs the SPAs may be redirected to after sign-in. No wildcards.

AUTH_DEFAULT_REDIRECT_URI.text: Redirect used when the caller does not name one.

AUTH_TRUST_FORWARDED_FOR.text: Read the client IP from `X-Forwarded-For` for login throttling and device alerts. Only safe behind the gateway, which overwrites it.

AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_LOGIN_CAPACITY.text: Login attempts per window per client (in-memory, per instance).

AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_REFRESH_CAPACITY.text: Token refreshes per window per client (in-memory, per instance).

GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID.text: Google OAuth client id. Blank disables Google sign-in.

GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET.text: Google OAuth client secret. Blank disables Google sign-in.

INTERNAL_API_TOKEN.text: Shared secret for service-to-service `/internal/**` calls (`X-Internal-Token`). One value for every service; the same compromise-everything caveat applies.

SELLER_DATA_KEY.text: AES-256 key (base64, 32 bytes) that encrypts sellers' bank account numbers. **seller-service refuses to start without it**, or with a key that is not exactly 32 bytes.

KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS.text: Kafka brokers (`host:port,host:port`). On AWS the MSK plaintext listener, reachable only from the cluster.

SPRING_KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS.text: Same brokers for the shared audit-event publisher, which reads the Spring name.

STATIC_IMAGE_SERVER_URL.text: Where product-service reaches static-image-server to upload/delete product images (e.g. `http://static-image-server/product-images`). Blank disables the image upload endpoints; existing image URLs keep working.

STATIC_IMAGE_SERVER_PUBLIC_URL.text: Browser-facing base URL of the product images. Seeds the `parentUrl` setting on first startup only; after that `PUT /api/admin/image-settings` changes it at runtime without a restart.

STATIC_IMAGE_SERVER_TOKEN.text: `X-Image-Token` product-service sends on PUT/DELETE to static-image-server. Same value as `IMAGE_SERVER_TOKEN`.

IMAGE_SERVER_TOKEN.text: Write token static-image-server requires on PUT/DELETE (reads are public). Set in `deploy/local/.env`.

NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER.text: nginx image setting: only variables with this prefix (`IMAGE_SERVER_`) are substituted into the config template, so nginx's own `$variables` are left alone.

EMBEDDING_PROVIDER.text: Embedding provider for semantic product search (Cartwise AI-1): `none` (default, feature off, `GET /api/products/search` answers keyword-only with `degraded=true`), `bedrock`, or `fake` (deterministic non-semantic vectors, refused unless the `dev-fake` profile is active).

EMBEDDING_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID.text: Bedrock embedding model. Default `amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0`, called with 1024 dimensions. The vector column is `vector(1024)`, so a model with another width needs a new table and a cutover, not just this setting.

EMBEDDING_RECONCILER_ENABLED.text: `false` stops the background job that (re)embeds new and changed products. Search keeps using the vectors already stored.

AWS_REGION.text: AWS region of the Bedrock endpoint. Needed only when `EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=bedrock`.

AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID.text: Passed through from the developer's shell for local Bedrock use; leave unset otherwise. Never set on AWS, where IRSA supplies credentials. The identity needs `bedrock:InvokeModel`.

AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY.text: Pair of `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, passed through from the shell for local Bedrock use only.

AWS_SESSION_TOKEN.text: Session token for temporary local AWS credentials (SSO / assumed role), passed through from the shell.

REDIS_HOST.text: Redis host: auth-service user cache and the gateway rate limiter.

SPRING_DATA_REDIS_SSL_ENABLED.text: Use TLS to Redis. ElastiCache has in-transit encryption on, so this is `true` on AWS.

STRIPE_SECRET_KEY.text: Stripe secret key. Stripe is on when this is set. At least one of Stripe or Razorpay must be configured under the `prod` profile or payment-service refuses to start; with neither it runs SIMULATED locally.

STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY.text: Stripe publishable key, handed to the browser.

STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET.text: Signing secret of the Stripe webhook endpoint.

MAIL_HOST.text: SMTP server. Locally the Mailpit container; on AWS `email-smtp.<region>.amazonaws.com` (SES).

MAIL_PORT.text: SMTP port (587 with STARTTLS, 465 with SSL).

MAIL_USERNAME.text: SMTP user. On AWS, the SES SMTP credentials Terraform creates.

NOTIFICATION_SENDER.text: From address of outgoing mail. Must belong to a verified SES identity on AWS.

NOTIFICATION_SERVICE_URL.text: Direct URL of notification-service. Blank resolves it through service discovery.

NOTIFICATION_SMS_MAILBOX_DOMAIN.text: Dev-only: SMS text is also emailed to `sms+<digits>@<domain>` so it shows up in Mailpit. **Blank in production**, which disables the sink; there is no SMS provider, so SMS is not delivered.

SPRING_MAIL_PROPERTIES_MAIL_SMTP_AUTH.text: SMTP authentication on/off. `true` with a real provider.

SPRING_MAIL_PROPERTIES_MAIL_SMTP_STARTTL.text: Upgrade the SMTP connection with STARTTLS (port 587).

VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY.text: Browser-push public key. Blank: generated on first start and stored in the database.

VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY.text: Browser-push private key. Blank: generated on first start.

GATEWAY_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS.text: Comma-separated exact browser origins allowed to call the API. No wildcards (the refresh cookie needs credentials). **No default in `prod`.**

GATEWAY_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED.text: Turns the gateway's per-user / per-IP request limiter on or off.

GATEWAY_RATE_LIMIT_READS.text: Reads (GET) allowed per minute per user or IP.

GATEWAY_RATE_LIMIT_WRITES.text: Writes (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) allowed per minute per user or IP.

GATEWAY_RATE_LIMIT_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS.text: Number of trusted proxies in front of the gateway (CloudFront + ALB = 2). The client IP is read that many entries from the right of `X-Forwarded-For`. 0 = use the socket address.

EUREKA_CLIENT_ENABLED.text: Register with and read from Eureka. `false` on AWS, where discovery is a Kubernetes ConfigMap plus Services.

EUREKA_INSTANCE_HOSTNAME.text: Hostname the Eureka server advertises. No default in `prod`.

ORDER_RISK_VELOCITY_THRESHOLD.text: Orders in a short window that trigger a velocity risk flag (Compose default 8). Mapped by Spring onto `order.risk.*`.

ORDER_RISK_AVG_MIN_ORDERS.text: Minimum past orders before the "unusually large order" check applies (Compose default 3).

ORDER_RISK_AVG_MULTIPLIER.text: How many times the customer's average an order may be before it is flagged (Compose default 10).

USER_REFERRAL_REWARD_COINS.text: Coins awarded for a successful referral.

TRACING_SAMPLING_PROBABILITY.text: Fraction of requests traced (0 to 1). 0.1 in production, 1.0 in local Compose.

OTEL_TRACES_ENDPOINT.text: OTLP/HTTP trace endpoint. Jaeger locally and in the AWS chart.

CART_JWKS_URI.text: Fixed URL of auth-service's public keys, used by cart to verify tokens. Set it on AWS (`http://auth-service:8081/.well-known/jwks.json`); blank resolves auth-service through discovery.

CART_JWKS_SERVICE_ID.text: Service id used to find auth-service when no fixed JWKS URL is set (default `AUTH-SERVICE`).

GATEWAY_JWKS_URI.text: Fixed URL of auth-service's public keys, used by gateway to verify tokens. Set it on AWS (`http://auth-service:8081/.well-known/jwks.json`); blank resolves auth-service through discovery.

GATEWAY_JWKS_SERVICE_ID.text: Service id used to find auth-service when no fixed JWKS URL is set (default `AUTH-SERVICE`).

INVENTORY_JWKS_URI.text: Fixed URL of auth-service's public keys, used by inventory to verify tokens. Set it on AWS (`http://auth-service:8081/.well-known/jwks.json`); blank resolves auth-service through discovery.

INVENTORY_JWKS_SERVICE_ID.text: Service id used to find auth-service when no fixed JWKS URL is set (default `AUTH-SERVICE`).

NOTIFICATION_JWKS_URI.text: Fixed URL of auth-service's public keys, used by notification to verify tokens. Set it on AWS (`http://auth-service:8081/.well-known/jwks.json`); blank resolves auth-service through discovery.

NOTIFICATION_JWKS_SERVICE_ID.text: Service id used to find auth-service when no fixed JWKS URL is set (default `AUTH-SERVICE`).

ORDER_JWKS_URI.text: Fixed URL of auth-service's public keys, used by order to verify tokens. Set it on AWS (`http://auth-service:8081/.well-known/jwks.json`); blank resolves auth-service through discovery.

ORDER_JWKS_SERVICE_ID.text: Service id used to find auth-service when no fixed JWKS URL is set (default `AUTH-SERVICE`).

PAYMENT_JWKS_URI.text: Fixed URL of auth-service's public keys, used by payment to verify tokens. Set it on AWS (`http://auth-service:8081/.well-known/jwks.json`); blank resolves auth-service through discovery.

PAYMENT_JWKS_SERVICE_ID.text: Service id used to find auth-service when no fixed JWKS URL is set (default `AUTH-SERVICE`).

PRODUCT_JWKS_URI.text: Fixed URL of auth-service's public keys, used by product to verify tokens. Set it on AWS (`http://auth-service:8081/.well-known/jwks.json`); blank resolves auth-service through discovery.

PRODUCT_JWKS_SERVICE_ID.text: Service id used to find auth-service when no fixed JWKS URL is set (default `AUTH-SERVICE`).

PROMOTION_JWKS_URI.text: Fixed URL of auth-service's public keys, used by promotion to verify tokens. Set it on AWS (`http://auth-service:8081/.well-known/jwks.json`); blank resolves auth-service through discovery.

PROMOTION_JWKS_SERVICE_ID.text: Service id used to find auth-service when no fixed JWKS URL is set (default `AUTH-SERVICE`).

RATING_JWKS_URI.text: Fixed URL of auth-service's public keys, used by rating to verify tokens. Set it on AWS (`http://auth-service:8081/.well-known/jwks.json`); blank resolves auth-service through discovery.

RATING_JWKS_SERVICE_ID.text: Service id used to find auth-service when no fixed JWKS URL is set (default `AUTH-SERVICE`).

SELLER_JWKS_URI.text: Fixed URL of auth-service's public keys, used by seller to verify tokens. Set it on AWS (`http://auth-service:8081/.well-known/jwks.json`); blank resolves auth-service through discovery.

SELLER_JWKS_SERVICE_ID.text: Service id used to find auth-service when no fixed JWKS URL is set (default `AUTH-SERVICE`).

SUPPORT_JWKS_URI.text: Fixed URL of auth-service's public keys, used by support to verify tokens. Set it on AWS (`http://auth-service:8081/.well-known/jwks.json`); blank resolves auth-service through discovery.

SUPPORT_JWKS_SERVICE_ID.text: Service id used to find auth-service when no fixed JWKS URL is set (default `AUTH-SERVICE`).

USER_JWKS_URI.text: Fixed URL of auth-service's public keys, used by user to verify tokens. Set it on AWS (`http://auth-service:8081/.well-known/jwks.json`); blank resolves auth-service through discovery.

USER_JWKS_SERVICE_ID.text: Service id used to find auth-service when no fixed JWKS URL is set (default `AUTH-SERVICE`).

RAZORPAY_KEY_ID.text: Razorpay key id (`rzp_test_...` / `rzp_live_...`), handed to the browser. Razorpay is on only when this and `RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET` are both set. INR payments only.

RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET.text: Razorpay key secret. Used server side for the API and to verify the checkout signature. Never sent to the browser.

RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET.text: Secret of the Razorpay webhook (`<site>/api/payments/webhook/razorpay`, events `payment.captured` and `order.paid`). Without it the webhook is rejected and payments settle only through the browser callback and the order-page re-check.

RAZORPAY_BASE_URL.text: Razorpay API base URL. Change only to point at a mock server in tests.

PAYMENT_DEFAULT_PROVIDER.text: `STRIPE` or `RAZORPAY`: the provider preselected at checkout when both are configured. Blank means the first configured one (Stripe, then Razorpay). Customers can switch before paying.

INVENTORY_DEFAULT_STOCK_QUANTITY.text: Stock given to a product or variant that has no stock row when product-service's catalog sync finds it. Default 0, so nothing is sellable until it is stocked; the local stack uses 100 so the demo catalog can be bought. Existing quantities are never changed.

INVENTORY_MISSING_STOCK_ROWS.text: `REJECT` (default): an order line with no stock row is out of stock. `UNLIMITED`: the old behaviour, where such a line could be oversold. Escape hatch only.

vite.VITE_API_BASE_URL: Origin of the API the admin app calls. On AWS it is the admin site itself (CloudFront forwards `/api/*`).
vite.VITE_APP_ORIGIN: Public origin of the admin app, used for OAuth redirects.
vite.VITE_ADMIN_URL: Link from the storefront footer to the admin site.
vite.VITE_AUTH_BASE_URL: Origin the storefront uses to start Google sign-in (`/oauth2/authorization/google`). On AWS the storefront origin. The admin app reads it too: Google sign-in starts there (default `http://localhost:8081` in dev, the API origin in production builds).
vite.VITE_GOOGLE_SSO_ENABLED: Shows the "Continue with Google" button. `deploy.sh` sets it from whether `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` is filled in.
vite.VITE_STOREFRONT_ORIGIN: Admin app: the storefront origin, used only to build "Preview on storefront" links in the theme editor. Default `http://localhost:3000`.

deploy.AWS_REGION: Region for everything except CloudFront certificates and WAF (always us-east-1).
deploy.AWS_PROFILE: Named AWS CLI profile; blank uses the default credential chain.
deploy.ENVIRONMENT: Environment name; with PROJECT it names the environment and is the word `destroy.sh` asks you to type.
deploy.DOMAIN_NAME: Root domain you control. Serves `shop.`, `admin.` and `api.` subdomains.
deploy.SIZE_PROFILE: `lean` = cheapest working topology; `prod` = full high availability.
deploy.ALERT_EMAIL: Address that receives CloudWatch alarms (AWS emails a confirmation link).
deploy.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY: **One provider required.** Stripe secret key. Set all three Stripe values or none.
deploy.STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY: Stripe publishable key (all three Stripe values or none).
deploy.STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET: Signing secret of the Stripe webhook endpoint (all three Stripe values or none).
deploy.KUBERNETES_API_ALLOWED_CIDRS: Comma-separated CIDRs allowed to reach the Kubernetes API. Narrow it for production.
deploy.RESTRICT_ALB_TO_CLOUDFRONT: Only CloudFront may connect to the load balancer, so the WAF cannot be bypassed.
deploy.IMAGE_TAG: Image tag override; default is the git commit (plus a hash of uncommitted changes).
deploy.SKIP_FRONTENDS: `true` skips building and uploading the two web apps.
deploy.RAZORPAY_KEY_ID: **One provider required.** Razorpay key id. Set all three Razorpay values or none. You may configure Stripe, Razorpay or both.
deploy.RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET: Razorpay key secret (all three Razorpay values or none).
deploy.RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET: Secret of the Razorpay webhook endpoint (all three Razorpay values or none).
